title: Nasi Goreng Kampung
steps: Separate the cold rice grains with damp fingers and prepare all ingredients before heating the wok.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over medium-high heat for 45 seconds, then fry the anchovies for 2 minutes until crisp; remove and reserve.
Add the shallots, garlic, and chilli to the same wok and stir-fry for 60 to 90 seconds until fragrant without burning the garlic.
Add the choy sum stems first, cook for 1 minute, then add the leaves and cook for another 30 seconds.
Add the rice and stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes, pressing out any clumps, then add 1 tablespoon soy sauce around the edge of the wok.
Push the rice aside, scramble the eggs in the empty space for 60 seconds, then combine everything and return the crisp anchovies before serving hot.
image_alt: A bowl of Malaysian-style fried rice with egg and vegetables

title: Mee Goreng Mamak
steps: Rinse the yellow noodles briefly under warm water, drain thoroughly, and mix the chilli sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and 2 tablespoons water in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and brown the tofu for 3 to 4 minutes, turning until at least two sides are golden.
Add the garlic and choy sum stems; stir-fry for 60 seconds, then add the tomato and choy sum leaves.
Push the vegetables aside, add the eggs, and scramble for about 45 seconds until softly set.
Add the noodles and prepared sauce, increase to high heat, and toss continuously for 2 to 3 minutes until the noodles are evenly coated and steaming.
Taste one noodle, add 1 tablespoon water if the mixture is dry, and serve immediately while the vegetables remain slightly crisp.
image_alt: A wok-fried noodle dish with tofu, egg, and vegetables

title: Ayam Masak Kicap
ingredient_quantities: 400 g boneless chicken thigh, cut into 3 cm pieces
1 medium potato, cut into 2 cm cubes
steps: Pat the chicken dry, cut it into even pieces, and wash hands and the cutting board immediately after handling raw poultry.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 4 minutes, turning so at least two sides colour.
Add the onion, garlic, ginger, and chilli; cook for 2 minutes until the onion begins to soften.
Add the potato, sweet soy sauce, light soy sauce, and 150 ml water, then stir and bring to a gentle boil.
Cover, reduce to medium-low heat, and simmer for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring twice, until the potato is tender.
Check the thickest chicken piece reaches 75 C with no pink centre; uncover and simmer for 2 minutes to thicken the sauce before serving.
image_alt: Malaysian soy-braised chicken served with potatoes and rice

title: Kari Ayam Kentang
ingredient_quantities: 500 g chicken thigh, cut into pieces
2 medium potatoes, cut into 3 cm cubes
steps: Mix the curry powder with 3 tablespoons water to form a smooth paste and prepare the chicken and potatoes separately.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat; cook the onion for 4 minutes until translucent, then add garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the curry paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the oil begins to separate and the spices smell toasted.
Add the chicken and stir for 4 minutes until the outside is no longer pink, then add the potatoes and 300 ml water.
Cover and simmer on medium-low heat for 18 minutes, then add the coconut milk and salt without allowing a hard boil.
Simmer uncovered for 7 minutes until the potato is tender, the sauce coats a spoon, and the chicken reaches 75 C; rest for 5 minutes before serving.
image_alt: A bowl of Malaysian chicken and potato curry

title: Sambal Telur
steps: Place the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water, bring to a boil, and simmer for 9 minutes; transfer to cold water and peel.
Mix the tamarind paste with 100 ml water and set it beside the stove with the measured sugar and salt.
Heat the oil over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the chilli paste and cook for 3 minutes, stirring frequently, until it darkens slightly and no longer smells raw.
Add the tomato, tamarind water, sugar, and salt; simmer for 6 to 8 minutes until the sambal is thick enough to leave a trail when stirred.
Add the peeled eggs, turn them gently in the sambal for 2 minutes, and serve with rice.
image_alt: Boiled eggs coated in a red sambal sauce

title: Kangkung Belacan
steps: Wash the kangkung in two changes of water, drain well, and separate the thicker stems from the leaves.
Pound or finely chop the garlic, shallots, chilli, and belacan into a coarse paste.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat for 45 seconds, add the paste, and stir-fry for 60 to 90 seconds until fragrant.
Add the kangkung stems and 2 tablespoons water; toss for 1 minute.
Add the leaves and sugar, then stir-fry for another 60 to 90 seconds until wilted but still bright green.
Remove immediately from the wok to prevent overcooking and serve hot.
image_alt: Bright green stir-fried water spinach with chilli

title: Sup Sayur Telur
steps: Wash the vegetables, slice the carrot no thicker than 3 mm, and separate the choy sum stems from the leaves.
Bring the stock to a boil in a medium saucepan, add the garlic and carrot, and simmer for 4 minutes.
Add the choy sum stems and cook for 2 minutes, then add the leaves and soy sauce.
Reduce to a gentle simmer and slowly pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream while stirring once around the pot.
Leave undisturbed for 30 seconds, then stir gently to form egg ribbons and cook for another minute.
Add the white pepper and spring onion, taste before adding any salt, and serve immediately.
image_alt: A clear vegetable soup with egg ribbons

title: Fried Bee Hoon
steps: Soak the rice vermicelli in room-temperature water for 8 to 10 minutes until flexible but not soft, then drain thoroughly.
Mix the soy sauce, sesame oil, and 100 ml water in a bowl; prepare all vegetables before heating the wok.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil over medium-high heat, brown the tofu for 3 minutes, and remove it from the wok.
Add the remaining oil and garlic, stir for 30 seconds, then scramble the eggs until just set.
Add the carrot and choy sum stems for 2 minutes, then add the leaves, noodles, tofu, and sauce.
Toss over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the noodles are tender without becoming mushy.
image_alt: Fried rice vermicelli with egg, tofu, and vegetables

title: Tomato Egg Rice
steps: Beat the eggs with 1 tablespoon water and prepare the tomatoes before heating the pan.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil over medium heat, add the eggs, and fold for 45 to 60 seconds until softly set; remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and garlic to the pan and cook for 20 seconds without browning.
Add the tomatoes, sugar, soy sauce, and 2 tablespoons water; cover and cook for 4 minutes until the tomatoes release their juice.
Return the eggs and fold gently for 1 minute so they absorb the tomato sauce without breaking apart.
Divide the hot rice between two bowls, spoon the tomato egg mixture over it, and serve immediately.
image_alt: Soft scrambled eggs and tomatoes served over rice

title: Tauhu Goreng Kicap
steps: Pat the tofu dry and cut it into 2 cm cubes so the surface browns instead of steaming.
Mix the sweet soy sauce, light soy sauce, garlic, chilli, and 2 tablespoons water in a small bowl.
Heat the oil over medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 6 to 8 minutes, turning every 2 minutes until golden on several sides.
Reduce to medium heat, pour in the sauce, and toss for 60 to 90 seconds until it becomes glossy and coats the tofu.
Transfer the tofu to a plate and top with the cucumber and crushed peanuts.
Serve immediately so the tofu remains crisp; keep extra sauce separate if storing leftovers.
image_alt: Golden fried tofu with cucumber, chilli, and peanuts

title: Bubur Ayam
steps: Rinse the rice until the water is mostly clear, then place it in a large pot with the stock, ginger, and garlic.
Bring to a boil, reduce to the lowest simmer, and cook partly covered for 30 minutes, stirring every 8 minutes to prevent sticking.
Add the whole chicken pieces and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until their centres reach 75 C.
Remove and shred the chicken with two forks, then return it to the pot.
Continue simmering for 8 to 10 minutes until the rice breaks down and the porridge is creamy; add hot water if it becomes too thick.
Stir in soy sauce and white pepper, divide into bowls, and garnish with spring onion.
image_alt: Malaysian chicken rice porridge topped with spring onion

title: Sardin Masak Tomato
ingredient_quantities: 1 can sardines in tomato sauce, about 425 g
steps: Open the sardine can, keep the fish pieces whole, and mix the tamarind paste with 80 ml water.
Heat the oil over medium heat and cook the onion for 3 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and chilli and cook for 30 seconds, then add the fresh tomato wedges.
Pour in the canned tomato sauce and tamarind water and simmer for 4 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the sardines carefully, spoon sauce over them, and simmer for 3 minutes without vigorous stirring so they do not break apart.
Serve hot with rice and refrigerate any leftovers within 2 hours.
image_alt: Fish simmered in a tomato, onion, and chilli sauce

title: Nasi Lemak Quick Plate
steps: Rinse the rice until the water is nearly clear, then combine it with coconut milk, water, and salt in a rice cooker or covered pot.
Cook using the normal rice setting, or bring to a boil and simmer covered on low heat for 15 minutes; rest covered for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool them in cold water, peel, and halve.
Dry-fry the anchovies in a small pan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp, stirring frequently.
Warm the prepared sambal until steaming and slice the cucumber just before serving.
Fluff the rice and assemble each plate with egg, cucumber, anchovies, peanuts, and 2 tablespoons sambal.
image_alt: A Malaysian nasi lemak plate with egg, cucumber, anchovies, and sambal

title: Curry Mee
ingredient_quantities: 150 g tofu puffs or firm tofu
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool, peel, and halve; blanch the noodles for 30 seconds and divide between two bowls.
Mix the curry powder with 3 tablespoons water to form a paste.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and fry the curry paste for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the stock and tofu, bring to a gentle boil, and simmer for 6 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and choy sum and simmer gently for 3 minutes; do not boil hard or the coconut milk may split.
Taste and add up to 1/2 teaspoon salt, ladle the hot broth over the noodles, and top each bowl with egg.
image_alt: A bowl of Malaysian curry noodles with tofu, greens, and egg

title: Ikan Masak Asam
steps: Pat the fish dry, cut into large pieces, and mix the tamarind paste with 400 ml water.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 3 minutes, then add garlic and chilli for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato wedges and cook for 3 minutes until they begin to soften.
Pour in the tamarind water, bring to a simmer, and cook uncovered for 5 minutes.
Add the okra and fish in one layer, cover, and simmer gently for 6 to 8 minutes without vigorous stirring.
Check that the fish is opaque and flakes easily at the thickest point, add salt, and serve immediately.
image_alt: Fish and okra in a Malaysian sour tamarind broth

title: Masak Lemak Cili Api
ingredient_quantities: 450 g boneless chicken thigh, cut into pieces
steps: Blend or pound the chillies, garlic, turmeric, and 3 tablespoons water into a smooth paste.
Place the paste, lemongrass, and remaining water in a saucepan and simmer over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken pieces, stir to coat, and simmer covered for 12 minutes, turning once.
Add the coconut milk and salt and reduce the heat so the sauce only bubbles gently.
Cook uncovered for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring every 2 minutes, until the sauce slightly thickens.
Confirm the thickest chicken piece reaches 75 C, remove the lemongrass, and rest for 3 minutes before serving.
image_alt: Malaysian chicken in a yellow coconut and chilli sauce

title: Roti John
ingredient_quantities: 1 small baguette or 2 long bread rolls
steps: Split the bread lengthwise without cutting all the way through and mix the eggs, minced chicken, onion, and salt in a bowl.
Heat the oil on a flat pan over medium heat and spread the egg mixture into a rectangle the size of the bread.
Press the cut side of the bread onto the wet mixture and cook for 3 minutes until the egg is set underneath.
Flip the bread and cook for another 3 to 4 minutes until the chicken mixture reaches 75 C.
Transfer to a board, drizzle with chilli sauce and mayonnaise, and close the bread.
Cut into four pieces and serve immediately while the outside is crisp and the centre is hot.
image_alt: A Malaysian Roti John egg and chicken sandwich

title: Stir-Fried Choy Sum with Garlic
steps: Wash the choy sum thoroughly, drain, and separate the 4 cm stem pieces from the leaves.
Mix the oyster sauce, soy sauce, and 2 tablespoons water in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat for 45 seconds and fry the garlic for 20 to 30 seconds until pale gold.
Add the stems and stir-fry for 90 seconds, keeping them moving so the garlic does not burn.
Add the leaves and prepared sauce and toss for another 60 to 90 seconds until the leaves wilt but remain bright green.
Transfer immediately to a serving plate and serve hot; do not leave the vegetables in the hot wok.
image_alt: Garlic stir-fried choy sum served on a plate
